points.description: States the rule: the weight adjustment (change in synaptic weight) is proportional to the product of the error signal and the input signal of that synapse (e.g. Δw_kj = η e_k x_j, with learning rate η).
points.partial_credit: Half if only one of error or input is mentioned, or proportionality/product is stated vaguely without clear terms.

points.description: Explains that the rule is derived from / is based on the steepest (gradient) descent method, i.e. minimising the error (cost) by moving weights against the gradient.
points.partial_credit: Half if it only says the rule reduces/minimises error without naming steepest or gradient descent.

rubric.notes: Full marks: the weight change is proportional to error times the synapse's input, and the rule comes from steepest (gradient) descent. Give half for each idea that is vague or incomplete, such as naming only error or only input, or saying only that it minimises error. No marks for a different rule (e.g. Hebbian or perceptron rule) or unrelated content.
